output.proposal: HB No. 10761 seeks to create the National Coordinating Council for Education (NCCE) under the Office of the President as the primary whole-of-government mechanism for coordinating, aligning and monitoring education and workforce development reforms, in line with the National Education and Workforce Development Plan (NEWDP). It also seeks to institutionalize the coordinating functions of the existing Education and Workforce Development Group (EWDG) created under Administrative Order No. 36, series of 2025, which the Council would succeed.
output.alignment: As a government organization measure, the review should examine whether a statutory council is needed in place of the existing EWDG, how the NCCE's functions fit with the mandates of DepEd, CHED, TESDA, DOLE, DEPDev and other member agencies, and how the measure relates to the streamlining of the Executive Branch under the Government Optimization Act (RA No. 12231), which Section 9 (Rationalization and Convergence of Inter-Agency Bodies) expressly invokes through the Committee on Optimizing the Executive Branch. The bill aligns with the Human Capital Development priority area of the FY 2027 Budget Priorities Framework, particularly its focus on equitable access to quality education. No LEDAC Common Legislative Agenda item is identified for the measure.
legislative_history: HB No. 10761 was filed on August 12, 2026 by Representative Agatha "Agay" Cruz; it is pending at the filing stage, and later stages are not recorded.
Several other House bills in the 20th Congress also seek to create a National Coordinating Council for Education, namely HB Nos. 9132, 9573, 10697, 11217 and 11275.
No earlier-Congress version, Senate counterpart, substitute bill or committee report was identified.

output.salient_features:
HB No. 10761 seeks to create the National Coordinating Council for Education (NCCE) under the Office of the President as the primary mechanism for coordinating education and workforce development reforms. Its salient features are as follows:
a. Section 3 (Creation of the National Coordinating Council for Education) provides that the Council is created under the Office of the President as a high-level inter-agency body for strategic coordination, policy alignment, convergence planning and monitoring of education and workforce development reforms, consistent with the NEWDP.
b. Section 4 (Composition of the Council) provides that the President shall chair the Council, may designate the Executive Secretary or a Cabinet member as Vice Chairperson, and that the members are the heads of DepEd, CHED, TESDA, DOST, DOLE, DEPDev, DMW and DBM.
c. Section 5 (Powers and Functions) provides that the Council shall harmonize policies, plans, programs and performance targets, monitor NEWDP implementation, identify gaps in learner progression, recommend government-wide priorities to the President, coordinate a human resource strategy for the education sector, and strengthen the labor market and skills information system, among others.
d. Section 6 (National Education and Workforce Development Plan) provides that the NEWDP 2026-2035 shall serve as the initial strategic framework, and that the Council shall monitor, periodically review and coordinate the preparation of a successor plan in consultation with stakeholders.
e. Section 7 (Education and Workforce Data Governance and Interoperability) provides that the Council shall coordinate an interoperable education and workforce data architecture, preferring interoperability over new centralized databases and complying with the Data Privacy Act of 2012.
f. Section 8 (Technical and Inter-agency Mechanisms) provides that the Council may create technical working groups and similar bodies, while using existing inter-agency mechanisms where practicable.
g. Section 9 (Rationalization and Convergence of Inter-Agency Bodies) provides that the Council, with DBM, shall review existing education and workforce inter-agency bodies and may recommend their rationalization, without itself having power to abolish or reorganize any body.
h. Section 10 (Council Secretariat) provides for a Secretariat under the Office of the President, headed by an Executive Director with the rank of Undersecretary appointed by the President.
i. Section 11 (Transition from the Education and Workforce Development Group) provides that the Council shall succeed to the coordinating functions of the EWDG under Administrative Order No. 36, series of 2025, which shall cease to operate separately, with its records and resources transferred.
j. Section 12 (Appropriations) provides that initial funding shall be charged against the current appropriations of the Office of the President and funds available for the EWDG, and that continuing requirements, including Secretariat staffing, shall be included in the annual General Appropriations Act.
output.related_measures_policy: HB No. 10761 may be considered alongside HB Nos. 9132, 9573, 10697, 11217 and 11275, which also seek to create a National Coordinating Council for Education but differ in membership, in the Council's authority over agency budgets, and in the treatment of existing inter-agency mechanisms. The measure aligns with the Human Capital Development priority area of the FY 2027 Budget Priorities Framework. The review should assess the need to convert the EWDG into a statutory council under Section 11 (Transition from the Education and Workforce Development Group), the consistency of Section 9 (Rationalization and Convergence of Inter-Agency Bodies) with the streamlining mandate under RA No. 12231, the role assigned to DBM as a member and as a partner in the rationalization review, and the staffing and cost implications of the Council Secretariat under Section 10 (Council Secretariat).
